stories.title: ETHIOPIA: Sr. Medhin Tesfay, Receives the International Lorenz Werthmann Medal
stories.description:
By: Bezawit Assefa
In recognition of her faithful service to communities affected by hardship, war, and displacement, her effective leadership in humanitarian and development initiatives, and her genuine commitment to restoring dignity and hope to the poor and vulnerable, Sr. Medhin Tesfay, a member of the Daughters of Charity of the Ethiopian Catholic Church, has been awarded the prestigious Lorenz Werthmann Medal in Germany.
Rev. Fr. Ketema Asfaw, Secretary General of the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of Ethiopia and Mr. Bekele Moges Director of Catholic Caritas Ethiopia have extended their messages of congratulations and solidarity to Sr. Medhin Tesfay, who serves as Director of the Daughters of Charity Project Office in Adigrat under Catholic Caritas Ethiopia Adigrat.
Rev. Fr. Ketema Asfaw, Secretary General of the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of Ethiopia, conveyed heartfelt gratitude and congratulations to Sr. Medhin on behalf of all the Bishops of Ethiopia.
“This distinction is not only a recognition of Sr. Medhin’s dedicated service, but also a source of pride for the entire Catholic Church in Ethiopia. We pray that the Lord may continue to bless her and the mission of the Daughters of Charity, strengthening them in their witness of Christian charity and service to those most in need,” said Rev. Fr. Ketema Asfaw.
The Secretary General further noted that Sr. Medhin’s dedicated service to the people has been a living witness to the Gospel spirit of love expressed through concrete action.
In addition, this recognition serves as a strong encouragement to the mission of charity and humanitarian service carried out by the Daughters of Charity, while also affirming the fruitful and longstanding partnership between the Congregation and Caritas Germany.
The Lorenz Werthmann Medal is a distinguished award named in honor of Fr. Lorenz Werthmann, who founded the German Caritas Association in 1897. The medal is bestowed upon individuals who have made outstanding contributions in the fields of Christian charity, humanitarian service, and social justice.
Under the leadership of Sr. Medhin Tesfay, the partnership between the Daughters of Charity and Caritas Germany has implemented nine major humanitarian and development programmes since 2005, benefiting more than 145,000 people through life-changing assistance and sustainable development initiatives.

stories.title: UGANDA: Bishop Kibira Calls for Greater Christian Participation in Church Through Synodality
stories.description:
By Masereka Peter
The Bishop of the Diocese of Kasese, Rt. Rev. Francis Aquirinus Kibira Kambale, has called on Christians to strengthen their participation in Church affairs by working closely with parish administrators and the clergy in promoting the mission of the Church through synodality.
Bishop Kibira emphasized that effective Church leadership and evangelization require collaboration between the clergy and the laity, urging Christians to actively participate in parish activities and support their respective parish administrations.
In his speech at St. Egidio Kacungiro Pastoal Centre on the feast of all saints, Bishop Kibira who attributed the development at the centre to the unity and cooperation between the clergy and the laity encouraged the faithful to join various Church movements and associations, noting that these provide opportunities for spiritual growth, fellowship, service and active involvement in the life of the Church.
The Bishop explained that synodality calls on all members of the Church to walk together, listen to one another, share responsibilities and collectively advance the mission of evangelization.
He challenged Christians to move beyond being passive members of their parishes and instead take an active role in building vibrant Christian communities through prayer, unity and service.
Bishop Kibira also emphasized the important role of women in the life and mission of the Catholic Church, calling for their greater involvement in Church leadership, decision-making and evangelization.
The Bishop noted that the spirit of synodality calls for an inclusive Church in which every baptized person, including women, is given an opportunity to participate, share ideas and contribute to the mission of evangelization.
He encouraged women to actively participate in Church movements, associations and other pastoral activities while urging parish priests and administrators to create an enabling environment for their meaningful involvement.
He further called on Christians to embrace mutual listening, collaboration and respect for one another's gifts, noting that women have important contributions to make towards the spiritual and pastoral development of the Church.
Bishop Kibira stressed that building a truly synodal Church requires the active participation of all the faithful, adding that the mission of the Church cannot be fully realized when the contributions of any group, particularly women, are overlooked.
END

stories.description: One of the world's best-selling video games, "Grand Theft Auto V" owes much of its staying power to its online multiplayer version.
